hypotheses.text: In the dominant DEE119 cohort described by Leitao et al. (2026) (n = 35), episodic central hyperventilation (HP:0002883) is documented in between 35% and 60% of assessed patients (approximately 12 to 21 of 35 individuals), representing a recurrent discriminating signature of dominant spliceosomal U2 dysfunction.
hypotheses.rationale: Hyperventilation is recurrently reported in primary dominant RNU2-2 discovery reports (e.g., 3 of 5 patients in Chiu et al. 2026 and highlighted in Greene et al. 2025). Resolving whether this feature is present in approximately half of the 35 dominant cases in Leitao et al. establishes whether it is a core diagnostic sign versus an intermittent finding.

evidence.text: Chiu et al. (2026) reported that among 5 patients with dominant RNU2-2 DEE, 3 exhibited hyperventilation episodes and status epilepticus occurred in all 5.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).

evidence.text: Greene et al. identified recurrent dominant de novo RNU2-2 variants in 25 individuals and noted hyperventilation as one of the cardinal features characterizing the syndrome alongside microcephaly, hypotonia, and severe epilepsy.

source.title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with prominent epilepsy
source.quote: The disorder is characterized by intellectual disability, autistic behavior, microcephaly, hypotonia, epilepsy and hyperventilation. All cases display a severe and complex seizure phenotype.

hypotheses.text: Microcephaly (HP:0000252 / HP:0005484) is present in >=75% (at least 26 of 35) of dominant DEE119 individuals in Leitao et al. (2026), showing a significantly higher penetrance in dominant de novo cases than in recessive biallelic RNU2-2 cases.
hypotheses.rationale: Microcephaly is consistently identified across both dominant RNU4-2 and RNU2-2 cohorts, but whether its penetrance reaches >75% specifically within the dominant subcohort of Leitao et al. is critical for clinical prioritization.

evidence.text: Leitao et al. report 35 individuals with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants, demonstrating overlapping clinical features with frequent epilepsy (85% overall).

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: We report RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants... The clinical phenotype associated with dominant or biallelic RNU2-2 variants is characterized by neurodevelopmental delay, severe ID and epilepsy in 85% of cases

evidence.text: Nakano et al. (2026) report that recessive RNU2-2 syndrome patients present with intractable epilepsy, growth retardation, microcephaly, and skeletal abnormalities.

hypotheses.text: In the dominant DEE119 subcohort of Leitao et al. (2026), status epilepticus (HP:0002133) and focal/bilateral tonic-clonic seizures exceed 70% prevalence (>=25/35), whereas infantile epileptic spasms (HP:0012469) are present in fewer than 20% (<7/35), distinguishing dominant DEE119 from early-infancy recessive RNU2-2 encephalopathy.
hypotheses.rationale: Chiu et al. (2026) observed status epilepticus in 5/5 patients with dominant DEE119 with median onset of 24 months, while infantile spasms predominate in earlier-onset DEEs. Determining whether status epilepticus is similarly predominant in the 35 Leitao et al. dominant patients will refine the epileptic semiology profile.

evidence.text: In the Chiu et al. cohort of dominant RNU2-2 DEE, 5 of 5 patients developed status epilepticus with a median seizure onset age of 24 months and mixed focal and generalized seizures.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for brain MRI findings (such as hippocampal sclerosis or delayed myelination) across dominant versus recessive RNU2-2 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Chiu et al. (2026) identified hippocampal sclerosis in 3 of 5 dominant patients; comparing this directly to Leitao et al.'s 35 dominant and 91 recessive patients will establish if structural hippocampal changes are a specific imaging biomarker.

new_directions.question_text: Does the frequency of autonomic/respiratory dysregulation (hyperventilation vs central sleep apnea) differ between RNU2-2 position 4 and position 35 dominant variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Greene et al. established that dominant RNU2-2 variants recur specifically at positions 4 and 35. Comparing clinical tables between these two positional hotspots will clarify genotype-phenotype correlations within dominant DEE119.
